rulings.detail: 2024 goes MISSING and fillable; 2021 (0 filed months) should be flagged MISSING on the same basis. ZERO believable months in 2024 — nothing was submitted in any lane. rulings.rationale: Deciding fact: the published 12-month zero sits on a ZERO-month submission record with no NIBRS row in any year, so there is no measured month behind it at all and the '12 months' label is a pipeline default, not a measurement — the packet's own BLANK-AS-ZERO shape, an FBI-side printed zero for an agency that submitted nothing. rulings.detail: FIVE believable months: SRS filed 5 months of 2024 and recorded zero Part-I offences in them; the remaining 7 months are unmeasured, and the 12-month 'complete' label in BOTH the CIUS and SPUB lanes is a pipeline assumption because neither publication lane carries a period field. rulings.rationale: Deciding fact: only 5 of 12 months were filed, so the published figure is a partial record wearing a full-year label — but the zero INSIDE those 5 months is ordinary rather than anomalous, because at this agency's baseline of 2.7/yr the expected count over 5 months is 1.1 and P(0) ~33%. That is precisely why this is a token/partial record and not a fabricated zero: the village is genuinely very low-crime, it is genuinely still reporting, and the only defective element is the completeness claim over the 7 unfiled months. The peer-rate arm is weak for this ORI and must not drive the repair (own 2.7/yr against a 12.4/yr band), so the DUAL screen firing is not evidence of magnitude. rulings.detail: ONE believable month: SRS filed 1 month of 2024 with zero offences in it; the CIUS and SPUB 12-month labels are pipeline assumptions layered on that single month. A records system still emitting empty monthly batches after the agency stopped producing records is the only reading consistent with both halves of that record: a 496-person town does not run 25 Part-I offences a year and then exactly zero for four straight years (P ≈ 1e-40 at that base rate).

A 12-month zero resting on one filed month is a token record published as complete, and because uplift is multiplicative it cannot be repaired as a partial year (0 × 12 = 0), so the only usable repair is missing-and-fillable.

The 2024 zero sits on the thin-filing side of the agency's own pattern, so it is an exposure artefact rather than a crime-free year; a collapse in months filed is not evidence about crime.

Anchors: exposure-weighted own rate 7 offences / 18 filed months = 0.39/month → 4.7/yr (2018: 5 on 7 months; 2019: 2 on 11 months → 2.2/yr) and the peer/size band at 503.4/100k × 492 ≈ 2.5/yr.
